summary: Lassen NF, Lassen County CA; CCC cab built 1939, staffed to 1982, moved by late 1994 to Eagle Lake's Gallatin Marina as an interpretive site; NHLR-registered 1997.

facts.design: R5-C3 cab, 14 by 14 feet, built by the CCC in 1939
facts.status_note: Cab moved from the Dow Butte summit by late 1994 to the southern shore of Eagle Lake (Gallatin Marina area). No source describes what remains on the summit.

access.note: Forest Service describes the relocated cab as having interpretive signage on the southern shore of Eagle Lake. No source describes access restrictions for the cab.

visit.trail_note: Interpretive site on the southern shore of Eagle Lake, per the Forest Service and the NHLR. The summit where the cab stood is not described as open to visitors.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Lassen National Forest (Eagle Lake Ranger District cooperator)

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps on Dow Butte, R5-C3 cab
Engine crew from Bogard Ranger Station rebuilt the concrete stairs from the parking lot to the base of the tower
By December 14, 1994 moved to the Gallatin area; later described at Gallatin Marina on Eagle Lake
Registered October 15, 1997 as NHLR US 241, CA 8

corrections.current: None relocated (The lookout was moved to Eagle Lake.)
corrections.proposed: By December 1994 moved to the Gallatin area of Eagle Lake (Gallatin Marina); later listed at the southern shore of Eagle Lake
corrections.why: The one-line note reads as no move at all and gives no date or site. The 1994 item, the photo page and the Forest Service page supply both.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1994 item says the Gallatin area. The NHLR and Forest Service say Eagle Lake. Peakbagging places the cab at Gallatin Marina on Eagle Lake, so the sources agree.
NHLR gives 6,705 ft (2,044 m) for the summit site and Peakbagging gives 6749 ft. The story does not use either figure.

notes_for_editor: Current location is supported by three sources. The 1994 move date comes from a secondary quote of a newspaper item, which we did not see directly. The brief has two coordinate sets for the summit (NHLR 40.740525, -120.826906 and west_us_lookouts 40.74795, -120.83024); we used the NHLR set and did not verify the other. A search result mentioned a closed lookout tower on the Forest Service site; this is unconfirmed and not used. Check with the Eagle Lake Ranger District before any visit.
